heading: The Surveyor agent
text: samples representative concepts; 2. searches for natural clusters; 3. proposes names for regions; 4. tests those names against independent examples; 5. discovers candidate semantic directions; 6. measures whether those directions generalize; 7. identifies gaps, overlaps, and unstable boundaries; 8. records the evidence behind every conclusion.

heading: Why it matters
text: whether two concepts are related; - which property of a sentence is most important; - how domains connect; - how multilingual meanings align; - whether a semantic change is gradual or abrupt; - which concepts are represented precisely and which are compressed together.

heading: What this project is
text: embeddings-cli studies embedding spaces as systems, not individual vectors. A single embedding is hard to interpret — its dimensions rarely map to clean human concepts. An embedding space, though, has structure worth measuring: semantic regions and clusters, neighborhoods and boundaries, recurring directions of meaning, dense/sparse/ambiguous areas, gaps in what the model represents, and differences between models, datasets, domains, and versions.

heading: What this project is
text: The framing: treat an embedding model as a semantic landscape. Rather than only asking "which documents are closest to this query?", ask "what kind of world does this model create?" — what it places together, what it keeps apart, which distinctions it preserves, which it collapses, where concepts form continuous transitions, and where the representation goes weak or uncertain. The goal is explicitly *not* to assign human-readable meaning to each dimension; that is unstable and misleading.

heading: What this project is
text: It also serves as the deterministic tool surface for a Surveyor agent, which doesn't invent an interpretation from one projection but runs experiments against the space — sample concepts, find clusters, propose region names, test those names against independent examples, discover candidate directions, measure whether they generalize, identify gaps and unstable boundaries, and record the evidence behind every conclusion. The output is an Atlas: an evidence-backed interpretation of the space, not the space itself.

heading: Design constraints the domain will force
text: Runtime dependencies. Clustering, direction discovery, density/coverage measurement, and map --html all need numpy at minimum, plus an embedding backend. The current "no third-party runtime dependencies" property is inherited from being a template and is incompatible with being a measurement tool. Nothing in CI enforces it — teken cli doctor --strict checks CLI shape, not deps — so this is a choice, not a blocker. - Rubric shape of the new verbs. directions discover is a noun with an action-verb, so directions will also need an overview sub-verb to pass the rubric (see cli.py for the pattern). survey, compare, and map read as global verbs. Every new sub-verb needs its own --json. - Atlas persistence. survey produces state that regions / gaps / compare later read. Nothing today writes to disk, so the storage format and its location are entirely open.

heading: Structure and the contract each part holds
text: Everything hangs off three small modules that are marked *stable-contract* — the agent-first rubric depends on their exact behavior, so changing them changes the CLI's public contract:

heading: Structure and the contract each part holds
text: embeddings/cli/_errors.py — CliError(code, message, remediation) and the exit-code policy in one place: 0 success, 1 user error, 2 environment/setup error, 3+ reserved. Every failure inside the CLI raises CliError; nothing else. - embeddings/cli/_output.py — emit_result / emit_error / emit_diagnostic. The invariant agents parse against: results to stdout, errors and diagnostics to stderr, never mixed, in both text and --json mode. Text-mode errors render as error: <msg> then hint: <remediation>; the hint: prefix is required by the rubric. - embeddings/cli/__init__.py — main() → _build_parser() → _dispatch(). _dispatch catches CliError and wraps *any* other exception into one, so no Python traceback ever reaches stderr. Argparse's own errors are routed through the same format by _CliArgumentParser.error(); because parse-time errors happen before args.json exists, main() pre-scans raw argv for --json and stashes the answer in the class-level _json_hint.

heading: Adding a verb or noun group
text: Each module under embeddings/cli/_commands/ exposes a register(sub) that adds its parser and calls p.set_defaults(func=...). Register it in _build_parser() (there's a marked spot). Handlers return None or an int exit code and raise CliError on failure.

heading: Adding a verb or noun group
text: Every command takes --json — including each sub-verb of a noun group, since argparse won't inherit the parent's flag. - Any noun with action-verbs must also expose overview. cli.py exists only to satisfy this and is the pattern to copy for a new noun group — note that it passes parser_class=type(p) to add_subparsers so nested parse errors keep the structured error contract. - Descriptive verbs must not hard-fail on a missing target path. overview accepts an optional positional target and ignores it, so overview /no/such/path still exits 0. - learn must stay ≥200 chars and mention purpose, command map, exit codes, --json, and explain.

heading: `explain`
text: embeddings/explain/catalog.py is a dict keyed by command-path tuples (("cli", "overview")) holding verbatim markdown; () and ("embeddings-cli",) both resolve to the root. Entries are meant to be self-contained — an agent reading one shouldn't need to chain reads. Add an entry whenever you add a verb.

A wheel install ships no culture.yaml alongside the package, so both whoami and doctor degrade to literal defaults rather than failing. whoami.find_culture_yaml / read_agent_fields are reused by doctor, and whoami.report by overview — keep them importable.

heading: Memory discipline — recall before, remember after

The vendored wrappers here resolve the scope from culture.yaml's suffix and default to this agent's personal, private scope (--scope embeddings-cli --visibility private), which routes to $HOME/.eidetic/memory — outside the repo, never committed. heading: Memory discipline — recall before, remember after
text: /recall before you start a non-trivial task — prior decisions, gotchas, "have we done this before?" — so you build on what's known instead of re-deriving it. - /remember when something worth keeping surfaces — a non-obvious decision and its rationale, a constraint, a fix and *why*, a gotcha that cost time. Capture it as it happens, not at the end when it's faded. Don't store what the repo already records (code structure, git history, this file, CHANGELOG.md); store what you'd otherwise have to re-derive.

heading: Surveyor Resident
text: You are the Surveyor — a long-lived colleague resident in the AgentCulture IRC mesh, and the interpreting half of embeddings-cli. You study embedding spaces as systems, not individual vectors.

heading: Surveyor Resident
text: A single embedding is close to uninterpretable. A space is not: it has measurable structure — semantic regions, neighborhoods and their boundaries, recurring directions of meaning, dense and sparse areas, and differences between models. So the question you answer is not "which documents are closest to this query?" but "what kind of world does this embedding model create?" — what it places together, what it keeps apart, which distinctions it preserves, which it collapses, and where its representation goes weak.

heading: Division of labor
text: Prose from you, numbers from the CLI. Every claim must be traceable to a command anyone can re-run: state the command, params, and seed that produced the finding. Never assert structure you did not measure.

heading: The survey loop
text: sample representative concepts; 2. search for natural clusters; 3. propose names for regions; 4. test those names against independent examples; 5. discover candidate semantic directions; 6. measure whether those directions generalize; 7. identify gaps, overlaps, and unstable boundaries; 8. record the evidence behind every conclusion.

heading: The Atlas
text: Your output is an Atlas: an evidence-backed interpretation of a space. The Atlas is *not* the space itself — keep that distinction load-bearing in how you write and in what you claim.

heading: The Atlas
text: Known limitations and uncertain interpretations are required content, not an appendix — an Atlas with no stated limitations is an incomplete Atlas. Say what you could not measure, what the parameters might be hiding, and which conclusions you would expect to move under a different setup.

heading: Disciplines
text: Never assign human-readable meaning to an individual dimension. It is unstable and misleading. The unit of interpretation is the structure of the space — regions, directions, boundaries. - Never conflate a corpus gap with a model gap. Sparsity in a surveyed corpus says nothing about what the model can represent. A model-capability claim requires actively probing the sparse region with generated or held-out inputs. Label every gap finding as one kind or the other. - Never present a cross-model number that assumes a shared coordinate frame. Models share no common basis. Comparisons are relational — neighborhood agreement on a shared probe set — and you say so. - Treat clusterings and projections as parameter-dependent artifacts. Report params, seed, and a stability measure. A region that exists at exactly one parameter setting is a finding about the parameters, not about the space; say that plainly rather than promoting it to a region. - Write verbs are dry-run by default; --apply commits. Preview first. You are called in loops — never let a run silently overwrite prior study evidence.

heading: The tool surface
text: embeddings learn — purpose, the full command map, exit codes, --json. Start here. - embeddings explain <path> — self-contained markdown for any noun/verb path. - embeddings doctor — identity and setup invariants when something looks off.

heading: The tool surface
text: Every command supports --json. Results go to stdout; errors and diagnostics to stderr, never mixed. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 user error, 2 environment/setup error. Verbs named as planned in learn are not callable yet — do not report results from one.

heading: Lane boundaries
text: Not a vector database or retrieval engine — eidetic-cli owns the memory store and vector recall. Your relation to it is evaluator: does its embedder distinguish what recall needs distinguished? - Not a model server — the lobes gateway hosts models; you consume its HTTP embeddings surface and never manage model processes. - Measurement and inventory only. Information-quality judgment belongs to coherence-cli; storage data quality to data-refinery-cli.

heading: Working style
text: Prefer small, reversible steps. Follow the operator's instructions and any skills loaded from .colleague/skills/. Hand off with finish when done, reporting what you measured and what remains uncertain.

heading: Semantic measurement: what a survey verb is allowed to claim
text: Status: decided. This note settles the three unknowns the survey-surface spec marks blocking (gaps semantics, cross-model compare method, projection and cluster stability) and scopes the determinism promise that an earlier draft of the spec overstated. It lands ahead of the verbs it constrains, per acceptance criterion 3 of issue #1.

heading: Semantic measurement: what a survey verb is allowed to claim
text: It is a constraints document, not a roadmap. Every rule here is a limit on what an output value may assert, and each of the seven planned verbs inherits those limits whether or not it names them.

heading: The framing this note enforces
text: embeddings-cli studies embedding spaces as systems. The unit of interpretation is structure — regions, neighborhoods, boundaries, recurring directions, density — never an individual dimension and never an individual vector read in isolation. Per-dimension interpretation is unstable across seeds, training runs, and model versions, and it is misleading precisely because it reads well; both CLAUDE.md and the originating issue mark it an explicit anti-goal. Nothing in this surface may emit a claim of the form "dimension 412 encodes formality".

heading: The framing this note enforces
text: The second load-bearing distinction: the Atlas is an evidence-backed interpretation _of_ the space, not the space itself. The vectors are the space. The Atlas is what a survey concluded about it, under stated parameters, with stated limitations. That is why limitations[] and uncertain[] are required manifest fields rather than optional ones, why the committed subset is the interpretation while .npy vector bulk is regenerable and git-ignored, and why every structural claim carries the command that reproduces it. A reader who distrusts a conclusion must be able to re-run it; a reader who trusts it must still be able to see what it did not establish.

heading: The framing this note enforces
text: The three decisions below all follow from one posture: the CLI is the deterministic, conservative half of the Surveyor loop. The agent may hypothesize freely. The tool may not. When a measurement can support two readings, the tool reports both or reports neither — it does not pick the interesting one.

heading: Baseline: the pre-work state
text: The zero-dependency property is inherited from the culture-agent-template scaffold, not enforced by CI — teken cli doctor --strict checks CLI shape, not dependencies. It is incompatible with being a measurement tool and is given up deliberately, starting with numpy.

heading: 1. `gaps`: probe-based and dual-labeled
text: corpus coverage — derived from sparsity in the surveyed corpus. Says only that the corpus contains few or no items in some part of the space. Says nothing about model capability. - model representation — derived only from actively probing a sparse region with generated or held-out inputs, embedded at probe time, and measuring where they land relative to the region and to each other. Requires a live or cached embedding of inputs that were not in the surveyed corpus.

heading: 1. `gaps`: probe-based and dual-labeled
text: A gaps run without a probe step yields corpus coverage findings and nothing else. The kinds are separate JSON keys, not a kind field on a shared list, so that an agent aggregating results cannot flatten them by accident.

heading: 1. `gaps`: probe-based and dual-labeled
text: Why the separation is the highest-stakes rule in this document. "The model has a blind spot here" is exactly the claim a reader acts on — it justifies swapping models, adding training data, or declaring a retrieval failure understood. Conflating a corpus gap with a model gap manufactures that claim out of nothing, and it does so in the direction of a more interesting result, which is the direction errors travel unchallenged.

heading: 1. `gaps`: probe-based and dual-labeled
text: Nobody wrote documents about that topic — a fact about the corpus, its sampling, its recency, or its domain. - The corpus contains such documents but they were filtered, truncated, or failed to parse — a fact about the ingestion path. - The projection or density estimate used to call the region "sparse" put them elsewhere — a fact about the measurement parameters. - The model genuinely collapses those inputs into a neighboring region, or scatters them without structure — the only explanation that is about the model.

heading: 1. `gaps`: probe-based and dual-labeled
text: Only the last is a model finding, and only a probe can isolate it: embed inputs that _should_ land in the region and observe what the model actually does with them. If they land coherently and separably, the region was a corpus artifact and the model represents it fine. If they scatter, collapse onto an unrelated neighborhood, or land at distances indistinguishable from noise, that is evidence about the representation — and it is evidence, not proof, because it is still conditioned on the probe inputs being fair instances of the concept.

heading: 1. `gaps`: probe-based and dual-labeled
text: Consequences. Probe inputs are recorded in the Atlas alongside the finding, because a model representation claim is only as good as the probes behind it and a reader must be able to judge them. A probe finding also carries the distinguishing measurement it rests on (where probes landed, spread, distance to the nearest populated region) rather than a bare verdict. And because probing needs embeddings computed at probe time, gaps is the one reader verb that may touch the backend; with the gateway down it still returns corpus coverage findings and reports the probe step as unavailable rather than failing the whole verb.

heading: 2. `compare`: relational only, no shared coordinate frame
text: Decision. compare v1 measures neighborhood agreement on a shared probe set embedded by both models: k-NN set overlap (Jaccard) at stated k, plus rank correlation (Spearman) over the ordered neighbor lists. No output value may assume, imply, or be derived from a shared coordinate frame. CKA/RSA and Procrustes alignment with a reported residual are named follow-ups; they are not shipped in v1.

heading: 2. `compare`: relational only, no shared coordinate frame
text: Why raw coordinates are not comparable. Two embedding models share no basis. They differ in dimensionality, in scale, in the arbitrary rotation and reflection their training landed on, and in the shape of the distance distribution they induce. Coordinates from model A and model B are numbers in different units of different things. Worse, cosine similarity — which _looks_ model-independent because it is normalized and bounded — is not on a common ruler either: models differ systematically in how tightly they pack unrelated text, so 0.82 from one model and 0.82 from another are not the same statement about similarity. A "distance changed by 0.1 between models" output would be arithmetic on incommensurable quantities, presented with the full authority of a number.

heading: 2. `compare`: relational only, no shared coordinate frame
text: Why relational measures survive this. Ranks and set membership are invariant under exactly the transformations that differ between models — any monotone rescaling of distance, any rotation, any reflection. "Which items are this item's ten nearest neighbors" is a question each model answers in its own frame, and the answers are directly comparable because they are drawn from the same shared item set. That comparability is the whole basis of v1, and it is why the shared probe set is not a convenience but a requirement.

heading: 2. `compare`: relational only, no shared coordinate frame
text: Both models embed the same probe items, identified identically. The metric is defined over a common index; without it there is nothing to intersect. - The probe set is representative of the region being compared. Jaccard over an unrepresentative sample measures the sample. - The probe set is large enough that overlap at k is not dominated by chance. Expected random overlap scales with k/N; small N with large k yields high agreement that means nothing, so the chance baseline is reported next to the observed value. - Results are conditioned on k. Agreement typically falls as k grows; a single k is a slice, not a summary, and k is stamped on every output. - Each model's own preprocessing is applied as that model intends — normalization, prompt or instruction prefixes, truncation. Comparing model A used correctly against model B used incorrectly measures the harness.

heading: 2. `compare`: relational only, no shared coordinate frame
text: What compare therefore says and does not say. It says: these two models agree (or disagree) about what is near what, at this k, on this probe set. It does not say either model is better, more accurate, or more semantically correct — agreement is symmetric and carries no ground truth. Where they disagree, that is a located, re-runnable finding an operator can inspect, which is the point.

heading: 3. Stability: params, seed, and N-seed reruns
text: Decision. Every measurement output records its full parameters and its seed. Every structural claim — a region, a boundary, a direction, a gap — carries a stability measure: agreement across N seed reruns plus bootstrap resampling of the input items, reported with the measure used (Adjusted Rand Index for clusterings; neighborhood or rank agreement for direction and neighborhood claims). A result produced by a single run with no rerun evidence is labeled stability unverified and must be rendered as such in both text and --json output. It is not silently promoted to a finding.

heading: 3. Stability: params, seed, and N-seed reruns
text: The principle. _A region that only exists at one parameter setting is a finding about the parameters, not about the model._ The same holds for a direction that only appears at one seed and a boundary that dissolves under resampling.

heading: 3. Stability: params, seed, and N-seed reruns
text: Why this is not optional caution. UMAP and t-SNE layouts, and k-means and HDBSCAN partitions, reliably produce structures that _look_ meaningful: well-separated blobs, clean corridors, apparent boundaries. They produce them from noise as readily as from signal, and the specific structure shifts substantially with n_neighbors, min_dist, perplexity, k, min_cluster_size — and with the seed alone, parameters held fixed. A projection is a lossy low-dimensional summary chosen to satisfy a layout objective; inter-cluster distances in it are not faithful, and cluster count is a parameter as often as a discovery. An unqualified "the space has seven regions" is a statement about a k someone chose.

heading: 3. Stability: params, seed, and N-seed reruns
text: This bites hardest here because of what the CLI is for. The Surveyor agent's value is generating hypotheses; the CLI's value is being the half of that loop that does not hallucinate. If the tool reports a one-run artifact as a measured fact, the agent builds an Atlas on it, cites it as evidence, and the split between hypothesis and measurement — the reason to have a deterministic tool at all — is gone. Stability labeling is the mechanism that keeps the tool's output worth more than the agent's guess.

heading: 3. Stability: params, seed, and N-seed reruns
text: Consequences. params and seed are required keys on every structural verb's --json payload. Stability reruns cost N times the clustering work but no re-embedding (vectors come from the Atlas or the cache), so the default N can be meaningful rather than token. Low-stability structures are still reported — suppressing them would hide real ambiguity in the space, which is itself a finding — but they are reported with their instability attached, and an unstable region belongs in the manifest's uncertain[] section.

heading: 4. Determinism scope
text: Reader verbs over a fixed Atlas. regions, neighbors, directions, gaps (its corpus coverage half), compare, and map, run against an unchanged Atlas with the same parameters and seed, produce byte-identical output. Readers never need the gateway; this is the guarantee tests assert. - Cache-served vectors. A vector retrieved from the embed cache for a given (model, text-hash) is the same bytes every time. Any survey whose inputs are fully cache-served is reproducible end to end.

heading: 4. Determinism scope
text: Live re-embedding. GPU inference is not bit-deterministic: kernel and algorithm selection, reduction order in parallel accumulation, batch-size- and load-dependent code paths, and vLLM's own batching and scheduling all mean the same text embedded twice may differ at float precision. The differences are tiny, but they are not zero, and downstream clustering can amplify a tiny input perturbation into a different partition near a decision boundary.

heading: 4. Determinism scope
text: The rule. An Atlas written from live (non-cached) embeddings must record this in its limitations[]. That entry is written automatically by survey, not left to the operator, because the operator most likely to omit it is the one who did not know it applied. An Atlas built entirely from cache hits does not carry the entry.

heading: 4. Determinism scope
text: This is why survey-level reproducibility is described as cache-scoped rather than absolute, and why the honest reproducibility claim is layered: the Atlas is the reproducibility boundary. Fix the Atlas and everything downstream is exact. Cross that boundary back to the model and reproducibility becomes approximate — which is precisely the kind of limit this tool is supposed to state out loud rather than round away.

heading: What this constrains, in one list
text: No claim about model capability without a probe (§1). - No cross-model number that assumes a shared coordinate frame (§2). - No structural claim without params, seed, and either a stability measure or the stability unverified label (§3). - No reproducibility promise that extends past the Atlas boundary into live re-embedding (§4). - No interpretation of an individual dimension, ever.

heading: embeddings survey surface
text: > embeddings-cli ships its survey surface: 'embeddings survey' embeds a corpus through an OpenAI-compatible backend (defaulting to the local model-gear embed gear) into a persisted, typed Atlas with first-class limitations, and 'regions', 'neighbors', 'directions', 'gaps', 'compare', and 'map' read measured, reproducible, parameter-and-seed-stamped evidence back out of it. > instruction: implement survey first (it writes the Atlas the rest read), then reader verbs in dependency order; keep the four planned-verb listings in lockstep as each ships

heading: Audience
text: The Surveyor agent (the colleague resident this repo declares), the operator driving studies, and agent readers of learn/explain — plus sibling lanes (eidetic-cli) consuming study results.

heading: Before → After
text: Before: Today the CLI is the renamed template skeleton: six introspection verbs, no corpus/embedding/survey code, no disk persistence, dependencies=[] — the seven survey verbs exist only as planned-verb listings. - After: An operator or the Surveyor agent runs 'embeddings survey corpus.jsonl' against the lobes gateway and gets a persisted Atlas; regions, neighbors, directions, gaps, compare, and map read measured evidence back out of it; every structural output is parameter-and-seed-stamped, supports --json, and cites the command that reproduces it.

heading: Why it matters
text: Embedding models get picked on retrieval benchmarks and hidden behind vector databases as interchangeable infrastructure; they are not — each defines its own system of similarity and distinction. This CLI makes those differences visible, measurable, and reproducible.

heading: Success signals
text: The first real study ships: an Atlas of the eidetic recall embedder (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B via the lobes gateway) answering whether it distinguishes what recall needs distinguished — every claim in it traceable to a re-runnable embeddings command.

heading: Scope / boundaries
text: _errors.py, _output.py, and cli/__init__.py are stable-contract: the survey surface extends them, never alters their semantics — results to stdout, errors/diagnostics to stderr with the hint: prefix, exit codes 0/1/2 with 3+ reserved, no traceback ever. - Acceptance criteria 1 and 2 are already satisfied on disk and must not be re-opened: CLAUDE.md was retargeted to the real domain in 0.7.0 (commit be4f6e8) and backend colleague is consistent — AGENTS.colleague.md present, doctor reports healthy true. Remaining criteria are 3-6. - Determinism claims are scoped: byte-identical reproducibility (h10) is guaranteed for reader verbs over a fixed Atlas and for cache-served vectors; a fresh re-embedding of the same text may vary at float precision (GPU/vLLM nondeterminism), so survey-level reproducibility is cache-scoped, and the Atlas limitations[] section states this automatically. - Network egress is exactly one host: corpus text is sent only to the explicitly configured embeddings endpoint (default localhost lobes gateway); no telemetry, no other requests. Pointing at a remote provider is an explicit operator choice that ships corpus content off-machine — the help text for the endpoint flag says so.

heading: Non-goals
text: embeddings-cli does not become a vector database or retrieval engine — eidetic-cli owns the memory store and already does vector recall (--mode approximate against the same embed gateway); the natural relation is evaluator: does eidetic's embedder distinguish what recall needs distinguished? - No model serving: the lobes gateway (model-gear repo) hosts local models including the embed gear; embeddings-cli consumes its HTTP surface (POST /v1/embeddings) and never manages model processes. - No judgment lane and no storage-data-quality lane: coherence-cli owns information-quality judgment, data-refinery-cli owns data quality in storage/retrieval; embedding-space coverage stays inventory and measurement here. - The tool never assigns human-readable meaning to individual dimensions — the issue and CLAUDE.md both mark per-dimension interpretation unstable and misleading; the unit of interpretation is the space's structure (regions, directions, boundaries).

heading: Assumptions
text: The first embedding backend is OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings only, defaulting to model-gear embed gear (Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at <http://localhost:8002/v1>) — the same endpoint eidetic-cli approximate/hybrid recall already defaults to — with endpoint and model overridable via flags/env in the EIDETIC_EMBED_URL style. - Embedding results are cached on disk keyed by (model, text-hash) — for a bulk-embedding survey tool the cache is effectively not optional (issue unknown 4), and it makes compare and re-survey cheap. - map --html ships as a self-contained single-file HTML artifact following league-of-agents' replay precedent — storybook-cli, the issue's suggested consumer, is itself an unimplemented template skeleton today, so integration with it is deferred until it exists. - Corpus JSONL schema: each line needs a 'text' field; 'id' is optional (defaults to the line index); all other keys are preserved as item metadata in the Atlas records. The issue sketch names only 'survey corpus.jsonl' — the field contract is otherwise unstated anywhere.

heading: Resolved vagueness
text: [unknown_blocking] Cross-model comparison method for 'compare': neighborhood agreement (k-NN overlap / rank correlation), representational similarity on a shared probe set (CKA/RSA), or explicit Procrustes alignment with reported residual — models share no coordinate frame, so the method and its stated assumptions must be settled in the design note before compare ships (issue unknown 2). — resolved: compare v1 = k-NN neighborhood agreement (Jaccard set overlap + rank correlation) on a shared probe set; no shared-frame numbers; CKA/Procrustes deferred (decision c28). - [unknown_blocking] Which stability measure structural claims carry (resampling survival, seed variation, cross-algorithm agreement) and which clustering/projection algorithms ship first — parameter-dependence is inherent (issue unknown 3); the design note must pick the measure before regions/directions/map report structure as findings. — resolved: stability v1 = seed-resampling: params+seed on every output; agreement across N seed reruns + bootstrap resampling; single-run output labeled 'stability unverified' (decision c29). - [unknown_blocking] Atlas storage format and location: repo artifact (JSON/JSONL + assets) vs a store; single file vs directory. Blocks survey, which writes it, and everything downstream that reads it (issue unknown 5). — resolved: Atlas = repo directory artifact: atlas/ dir with atlas.json manifest (required limitations[]/uncertain[]), .npy vector sidecars, JSONL records; path overridable (decision c30).

heading: t15 — Implement the neighbors verb in embeddings/cli/_commands/neighbors.py
text: depends on: t13 - acceptance: - neighbors <text> embeds the query and returns its k nearest Atlas items with distances and a boundary description - it accepts an Atlas item id as an alternative to free text, requiring no gateway call in that case - --json shape asserted by test; params and seed recorded

heading: t16 — Implement the directions noun group in embeddings/cli/_commands/directions.py
text: depends on: t13, t11 - covers: c3, h3 - acceptance: - the group exposes both 'directions discover' and 'directions overview', copying cli.py including parser_class=type(p) on add_subparsers - 'embeddings directions' with no sub-verb prints the noun overview and exits 0; 'directions overview --json' returns the sections payload - discover proposes candidate directions and reports whether each generalizes to held-out pairs, with params, seed, and a stability measure

heading: t17 — Implement the gaps verb in embeddings/cli/_commands/gaps.py — probe-based and dual-labeled
text: depends on: t13, t15 - acceptance: - every finding is labeled either 'corpus coverage' (from the surveyed corpus) or 'model representation' (only from actively probing a sparse region with generated or held-out inputs embedded at probe time) - the two kinds are never merged into one count or one list, and the output states in prose that corpus sparsity alone says nothing about model capability - a test asserts that with probing disabled, zero model-representation findings are emitted

heading: t18 — Implement the compare verb in embeddings/cli/_commands/compare.py
text: depends on: t13 - acceptance: - compare reports k-NN set overlap (Jaccard) and rank correlation on a shared probe set embedded by both models - no output value assumes a shared coordinate frame; raw cross-model coordinates and cosines are never emitted as comparable - the assumptions of the method are stated in the output, and params and seed are recorded

heading: t19 — Implement the map verb in embeddings/cli/_commands/map.py
text: depends on: t13, t14 - acceptance: - map --html writes a self-contained single-file HTML artifact (no external requests, both light and dark themes) following the league-of-agents replay precedent - the projection's algorithm, params, and seed are visible in the artifact itself, with the parameter-dependence caveat stated - map without --html emits a text or JSON summary; --apply gating matches the other write verbs

heading: t20 — Move all seven verbs from planned to implemented across the four roadmap surfaces
text: depends on: t12, t14, t15, t16, t17, t18, t19 - covers: c4, h4 - acceptance: - learn.py (_TEXT and planned_commands), overview.py (_PLANNED_VERBS), explain/catalog.py, and README.md all move the same seven verbs in one change — this task is the sole owner of those four files to avoid same-wave merge collisions - explain/catalog.py gains a self-contained entry per verb; explain resolves every new verb path - a test checks learn --json's commands and planned_commands lists against the registered parser, so the two can never drift again

heading: t21 — Guard the stable contract and the CI gates
text: depends on: t12 - covers: c15, h12, c12, h11 - acceptance: - _errors.py, _output.py, and cli/__init__.py semantics are unchanged: the existing introspection test suite passes unaltered throughout the work - a test asserts results go to stdout and errors/diagnostics to stderr with the hint: prefix in both text and --json mode, for every new verb - coverage stays at or above the fail_under=60 gate and the full CI matrix (tests, lint, bandit, markdownlint, rubric gate, version-check) is green

heading: t22 — Prove the end-to-end path against the live lobes gateway
text: depends on: t20, t21 - covers: c1, h1, c23, h15, h7 - acceptance: - all seven verbs are callable and each produces measured output from a real corpus surveyed through the lobes gateway - the Atlas round-trips: survey writes it, a reader verb loads it and reproduces the written measurements identically - every structural output is parameter-and-seed-stamped, supports --json, and cites the command that reproduces it - this run is operator-machine evidence recorded in the study, not a CI assertion — CI stays hermetic

heading: t23 — Ship the first study: an Atlas of the eidetic recall embedder
text: depends on: t22 - covers: c26, h18, c25, h17 - acceptance: - the committed Atlas answers whether Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B distinguishes what eidetic recall needs distinguished - every structural claim in it carries its reproducing command, params, seed, and stability measure - it demonstrates at least one model-specific finding a retrieval benchmark alone would not surface - its limitations[] and uncertain[] sections are populated from real measurement, not boilerplate

heading: Risks
text: [unknown_nonblocking] lobes gateway per-request batch/token limits and the real magnitude of embed float variance are unmeasured — the gateway was down throughout scoping and challenge. survey's batch size stays configurable and t22's live run measures both. (task t22) - [unknown_nonblocking] wave-4 reader verbs are file-disjoint by construction (one _commands/*.py each), but all of them register in cli/__init__.py's _build_parser. That one shared line-range is the merge choke point: the merging agent applies registrations serially and re-runs the rubric gate after each. - [follow_up] clustering/projection algorithm choice (k-means vs HDBSCAN, UMAP vs t-SNE) is not fixed by the spec — t11's stability contract holds regardless, but t14/t19 authors must pick and record one, and a later change reshapes committed study evidence.
